description: Examine a for loop and if statement written without braces on the if body and with uneven indentation.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Read the loop for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) on line 1. Read the inner if (i%2 == 0 && i%3 == 0) on line 2. Line 2 has no opening curly brace, and the indentation jumps left and right.
Without curly braces after if (...), Java treats only the single statement on line 3 as the body of the if statement.

steps.answer: Without braces, only the first statement on line 3 belongs to the if. A second statement below it would belong to the outer for loop and execute on all 100 iterations.
steps.question: If you added a second System.out.println line right below line 3 without adding curly braces around the if body, how many times would that second line print?

steps.description: See line 3 execute on i = 0 when both i%2 == 0 and i%3 == 0 are true.

title: Why Omitted Braces and Misaligned Indentation Cause Bugs
